column1: # R1664 — the surfaces whose OPENING screen routes no press anywhere, and why.
# `scene/pointer_reach` answers `dead_to_a_pointer` when a surface registers
# widgets and not one of them can receive a press: no painted tag carries a
# name the §5.35 router resolves, so every press in the window is dropped in
# silence. That is a total failure of a screen, and R1663 shipped one -- 185
# painted tags, an empty `shadows` list, an empty `unreachable` list, and a
# person pressing the window getting nothing. The boot gate now refuses it.
# It is refused for every example EXCEPT the ones listed here. A row is a
# claim that the surface has nothing to route a press to *in the state it
# opens in*, and the reason is what makes that claim reviewable. Adding a row
# to make a failure go away is the one use that turns this ratchet back into a
# suggestion; the repair for a real one is to paint the widget's surface under
# the tag it is registered with, which `scene/pointer_reach`.externals names.
# Measured 2026-08-12 over all 224 example packages: 206 answered, 9 could not
# be booted headless here (the same set the ink budgets record, for the same
# reasons), and NINE routed nothing. Every one of the nine was then checked
# against its own `$schema` and its paint, and none is the failure this gate
# exists for -- which is why they are rows and not repairs.
# ★ The gate is deliberately state-blind here, and that is why this file has to
# exist at all: `hello-contextmenu` is a live, driveable screen whose widget is
# painted only after a right-click, so at boot it is indistinguishable from a
# screen that is dead. The same shape as docs/containment-budget.tsv's, one
# axis over -- see debt-the-containment-gate-asks-once-at-boot.
# `<example>\t<reason>`. A surface not listed must route a press.
